title: Most Expensive Item That Can Not Be Bought
summary: Given two distinct prime numbers, primeOne and primeTwo, Alice and Bob visit a market with an infinite number of items, each priced with a positive integer.
statement: Given two distinct prime numbers, primeOne and primeTwo, Alice and Bob visit a market with an infinite number of items, each priced with a positive integer. Alice can use an infinite number of coins in denominations of primeOne and primeTwo to purchase items. She aims to determine the highest-priced item she cannot purchase to gift to Bob. The task is to return the price of this item.
constraints: primeOne and primeTwo are distinct primes and unlimited coins of both values are available.
An item is buyable when its price is a nonnegative combination of the two denominations.
Return the greatest positive price that is not buyable.
hints: For coprime denominations p and q, the Frobenius number is pq-p-q.
Every larger integer has a nonnegative representation, while this value cannot have one modulo either denomination.
editorial: Every larger integer has a nonnegative representation, while this value cannot have one modulo either denomination.

tests.explanation: Prices one and three are unreachable, and three is the greatest.
Seven is the Frobenius number for denominations three and five.
